subject: Bespoke retention & decommissioning timelines — order form language
messages:
From: Maya Li <maya.li@oceanichealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@oceanichealth.com
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood - bespoke retention windows + deletion proof for order form

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Oceanic Health leadership liked the latency and regional routing options. Before we move to procurement, our compliance team needs firm language in the Order Form around data residency, retention windows for PII-derived artifacts, and the deletion timeline once we terminate the service. A few specifics they flagged: 

- We need an explicit retention window option (we're asking about 7 years vs 3 years) for user-generated content and embeddings tied to PHI/PII.
- We need the maximum time-to-delete for active+passive copies (including backups and snapshots) after termination or contract non-renewal — Compliance is asking for a hard SLA.
- Proof-of-deletion: what evidence can Redwood provide (audit logs, signed attestation, deletion report)?

Can you share suggested Order Form wording and any limitations (e.g., backup retention rollback windows, legal hold exceptions)? Attaching our standard evidence checklist to this thread.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to finalize by July 20.

Best,
Maya
Oceanic Health — Senior Compliance Manager

Attachments: Oceanic_evidence_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: maya.li@oceanichealth.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood - bespoke retention windows + deletion proof for order form

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (sales lead) and Rishi (legal) to propose concrete Order Form language and to confirm what we can commit to operationally.

High-level notes from my side:
- Redwood supports per-customer retention windows configurable at onboarding. We can propose a 3- or 7-year retention tier. 7 years is available but may require the Dedicated / Private offering depending on data residency controls.
- Deletion timeline: for primary data we can commit to deletion within X days post-termination (see proposed draft below). Backups and offline snapshots typically require an additional short window (we track and can reduce it from our default).
- Proof-of-deletion: we can provide deletion reports (timestamped) and an attestation signed by our security lead. For some infrastructure-level copies (cloud provider snapshots) there are constraints — Rishi will outline risk language.

I'll attach an Order Form draft with redlines once we have alignment. Karthik/Rishi, can you advise on acceptable SLA phrasing and any commercial implications for a 7-year retention commitment?

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_Draft_OceanicHealth.pdf (draft stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, maya.li@oceanichealth.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed Order Form language and pricing impact for 7-year retention

Hi all — quick proposal for the Order Form and the commercial trade-offs. Draft language (to be inserted into the Order Form / SLA):

"Retention and Deletion. Customer may elect a retention window of 3 years or 7 years for Customer Data as defined in the Agreement. Upon expiration or earlier termination of the Agreement, Redwood will initiate deletion of Customer Data within thirty (30) days for primary storage. For backups and immutable snapshots, Redwood will complete deletion within one hundred and eighty (180) days, subject to the limitations below. Redwood will provide a Deletion Report and a signed Deletion Attestation within thirty (30) days of completion of deletion."

Commercial notes: a 7-year retention tier is available as an add-on (annual per-GB fee) because it increases storage and compliance overhead. If Oceanic requires Private deployment or isolated Dedicated pools (for regionally isolated backups), that will be reflected in the pricing schedule.

If that wording is acceptable to Compliance, we can produce a redlined Order Form.

—Karthik
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, maya.li@oceanichealth.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed Order Form language and pricing impact for 7-year retention

Thanks Karthik — a few legal redlines and clarifications we should add before committing: 

1) Delete vs. render inaccessible: for certain cloud-provider managed immutable copies, our operational path may involve cryptographic erasure or rendering data inaccessible prior to provider garbage collection. We should avoid promising physical media disposal where we cannot control the provider. Suggested tweak: 
"Redwood will render Customer Data inaccessible and, where feasible, complete physical deletion in accordance with the timelines above. Redwood will document the method of deletion performed in the Deletion Report."

2) Legal holds / subpoenas: add an exception clause that pauses deletion where Redwood is subject to a legal hold or where Customer has placed a hold via an agreed process. Include an SLA for notice (we'll notify Customer within 5 business days if deletion is delayed for legal reasons).

3) Proof/evidence: Deletion Report should include timestamps, SHA-256 hashes of affected objects (where applicable), the method used (e.g., logical delete, cryptographic key destruction), and the identity of the operator/automation that executed the action. We can provide an attestation signed by Redwood's Head of Security annually or on-demand at time of deletion.

4) Backup retention exceptions: some cross-region disaster recovery replicas may have a longer retention due to provider replication windows. We should list maximums explicitly if oceanic needs a hard cap.

I suggest we produce two redlines: one minimal (meets compliance expectations) and one strict (customer-favorable) with the pricing delta called out. Laura/Karthik — I'll attach a tracked-change doc with the exact clause text.

Rishi
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Retention_SLA_track_changes.docx (tracked changes stub)

2) We need the Deletion Report and Attestation to be issued to our security mailbox (compliance@oceanichealth.com) automatically upon completion.

If you can update the draft Order Form with Rishi's language and the 120-day backup cap as an optional checkbox (with the associated pricing delta), procurement will sign off and request DocuSign.
